tasks.short: Maintain health record indexes and storage systems

steps.what: Verify record identity, provenance and indexing fields before filing
Maintain health record indexes and store records under verified metadata
Check retrieval results, resolve filing exceptions and correct the index traceably

tasks.design: Configure metadata reuse, filing rules and exact-field search in the existing {OTHER} health record system. The specialist verifies identity and classification inputs before filing and retains exception resolution and retrieval checks; no clinical classification is inferred from prose.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same verified metadata is repeatedly entered across indexes or storage views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata fields and filing rules can reuse established values with audit trails.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong-patient records, duplicates and ambiguous document classes need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognizes when a plausible metadata match is unsafe or incomplete.
tasks.altitude: Focus record maintenance on identity integrity and retrieval quality rather than duplicate entry.

reach.task: Resolve ambiguous index categories and duplicate identities
reach.learn: Local record taxonomy and correction authority

evidence.claim: Reusing verified metadata across native record views can reduce duplicate entry; the proposed saving is E1.
Medical dossier retention and access accountability apply in the Dutch context described by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is index and storage maintenance, excluding original clinical documentation, diagnostic coding, episode-document processing and individual retrieval requests. A role roll-up must assign overlapping filing work once.

The specialist produces or verifies patient ID, encounter ID, document type, source, author, date, record version and access category in s1 with all 35 hours retained. Uncertain identity or category is held for manual clarification; no free structured classifier is assumed.

s2's ten remaining hours cover mapping checks and filing exceptions; s3 retains 25 hours for retrieval tests, corrections and unresolved cases. No automatic merge, deletion or retention-period decision is introduced.
Test native indexing and metadata reuse first; existing automatic filing yields no new saving. Missing metadata is entered manually and unsupported integrations remain manual.
unknowns: Record taxonomy and available native filing rules
research_questions: Does test filing preserve identity, provenance, version and retrievability across supported record types?

incremental.description: Maintain index mappings, audit checks and access settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+10+25=70; gross 30%, less 4 upkeep gives net 26%. Low 0 for existing automatic filing or high metadata correction effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check patient admission or discharge documents and verify required episode fields
Process admission or discharge documents by reusing verified fields in required forms
Resolve missing information and reconcile the completed admission or discharge record

tasks.design: Use native episode-linked forms in {OTHER} to reuse verified administrative fields while retaining source documents in {DOCS}. The specialist keeps first capture, completeness checks and clarification through {EMAIL}; the change does not make an admission or discharge decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified episode details are copied into multiple required forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native form population and explicit required-field checks can reduce copying without interpreting clinical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Missing signatures, conflicting dates and ambiguous source documents need the responsible staff to clarify them.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes an administrative omission from a clinical fact that cannot be guessed.
tasks.altitude: Process paperwork with a single checked administrative entry and visible exceptions.

reach.task: Clarify episode dates and missing source documents
reach.learn: Document ownership and which facts require clinician confirmation

evidence.claim: Native episode-linked forms can reuse verified administrative fields; this is an unmeasured E1 design.

assumptions: Boundary is administrative processing of received documents; clinical decisions, document authoring, diagnostic coding and general archive maintenance are excluded. Overlapping filing time must be assigned once.

Clinical and ward staff produce source admission or discharge documents in normal care. The specialist verifies or manually captures patient and episode IDs, event type, dates, author, document version, signature status and required attachment status in s1, retaining all 35 hours.
s2's 13.5 hours include field mapping inspection and manual completion where native reuse fails. No generated diagnosis, inferred discharge status or free document extraction is assumed.
s3 retains all 20 hours for reconciliation and queries. Existing clinical clarification work remains unchanged; extra demand beyond normal processing would reduce savings.
Test native form configuration first. Already prefilled forms earn no saving; unsupported forms remain manual.
research_questions: Can native reuse populate all tested forms without mixing episodes or overwriting corrected dates?

already_counted.description: Source checks and first field capture
Form checks, mapping exceptions and manual completion

incremental.description: Maintain form versions, mappings and completeness rules

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+13.5+20=68.5; gross 31.5%, less 4 upkeep gives net 27.5%. Low 0 for existing prefill or frequent manual source reconciliation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Retrieve medical records for authorized personnel

steps.what: Verify the medical-record request, patient identity, scope and requester authorization
Retrieve patient medical records using the verified scope and record index
Check retrieved records and provide the exact permitted package to medical personnel

tasks.design: Use saved exact-field searches and package views in the {OTHER} health record system after the request is verified. The specialist checks the retrieved contents and authorizes the exact permitted access through existing secure channels; there is no broad search exposure or automated disclosure.
tasks.previous_blocker: A verified request can require repeated searches across record views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native patient, episode and document-type filters can assemble a scoped package without semantic interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong-patient matches, restricted records and incomplete archives require review.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist checks that the package is both relevant and permissible for this requester.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time repeating searches while retaining disclosure responsibility.

reach.task: Clarify the episode and document scope needed for care
reach.learn: Request minimum necessary records with accurate identifiers

evidence.claim: Native scoped retrieval can reduce repeated record searches; the saving is E1 and assumes no existing equivalent view.
The Dutch dossier guidance includes retention and accountability for who has viewed the record.

assumptions: Boundary is a particular request through secure access delivery, excluding archive creation, general indexing and clinical use of the retrieved information.

The requester supplies the care-related request through the existing process. The specialist captures and checks patient ID, requested episode/date range, document classes, requester identity, purpose and permitted scope in s1 with all 30 hours retained. Unclear authorization is manually escalated rather than inferred.

Existing archive staff produce the record index through normal maintenance, with no new field capture required here. s2's 18 hours include search checks, paper or missing-record retrieval and exceptions; extensive paper retrieval reduces savings.

s3 retains 25 hours for content and authorization checks, secure handoff and positive approval. a1 binds the package manifest/version, patient, scope, requester and delivery route after retrieval; any change voids approval.
Test native filters first. Existing automatic retrieval earns no new saving, and recipient self-service work is not assumed.
unknowns: Archive fragmentation and paper record share
Native package search and access controls
research_questions: Does the package match independently checked patient, episode, scope and access permissions?

already_counted.description: Package check, approval and secure handoff

incremental.description: Maintain scoped search settings and audit access

approvals.approved_version: Exact record package manifest and version for verified patient, requested scope, requester and secure delivery route; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+18+25=73; gross 27%, less 4 upkeep gives net 23%. Low 0 with existing package views or predominantly paper retrieval. Authorization checks remain intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clarify conflicting or missing coding information with clinicians

steps.what: Identify unclear codes or diagnoses and assemble the conflicting source evidence
Consult doctors or attend coding meetings to resolve missing or conflicting information
Resolve codes using documented clarification or retain the unresolved query

tasks.design: Use linked evidence and a reusable clarification form in {OTHER} and {DOCS} to assemble the query pack. The specialist identifies the ambiguity, consults the clinician and applies the documented resolution; no model invents a missing diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clarification preparation repeatedly copies source excerpts and record references.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record links and query templates can reduce assembly without deciding the answer.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting documentation often needs a clinician's factual clarification and specialist coding judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist asks a precise, non-leading question and preserves unresolved uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Bring clearer evidence to coding discussions while retaining resolution judgement.

reach.task: Clarify the clinical facts underlying an ambiguous coding query
reach.learn: Ask for facts without suggesting an unsupported diagnosis

evidence.claim: DHD supports ICD-10 coding from day-admission clinical text; this is a coding capability and does not establish autonomous resolution of conflicting source diagnoses.
The proposed linked clarification-pack saving is an E1 estimate, not a coding accuracy result.

assumptions: Boundary is an identified coding ambiguity through documented resolution, excluding routine coding of clear records and unrelated retrieval requests. No saving in clinician consultation is claimed.

In s1 the specialist produces patient/episode references, disputed code or phrase, conflicting source versions and dates, relevant excerpts and the precise missing fact. Its 28 remaining hours include reading, capture, issue identification and checking links; no structured conflict flag is supplied for free.

The clinician produces clarification during the existing consultation in s2, with the specialist's full 45 hours retained. s3 keeps all judgement and traceable correction time. Unanswered questions remain open rather than becoming inferred codes.
Test native links and templates first; existing query-pack automation earns no new saving. No model loop or automatic clinical text synthesis is needed for this limited change.
unknowns: Native query links and clarification turnaround
research_questions: Does a linked pack reduce preparation without omitting contradictory evidence or increasing clinician clarification work?

already_counted.description: Issue identification, evidence capture and pack checking

incremental.description: Maintain query forms, links and access settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=28+45+15=88; gross 12%, less 3 upkeep gives net 9%. Low 0 with existing linked packs or unusually complex source review. No consultation or coding judgement is removed.

role.altitude: Reduce repeated field entry and evidence assembly while retaining identity checks, controlled access and coding clarification.
reach: Clarify missing clinical facts with doctors
Coordinate record integrity with records supervisors
role.ambitious_version: A records specialist who makes information easier to find and trace without weakening clinical uncertainty or access controls.
